entities.name: Suda
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Suda is a Byzantine lexicon created by various authors around 1000 AD. This comprehensive encyclopedia of the Byzantine era was a key source of information for scholars during the Middle Ages.

It contained extensive knowledge on various fields, including grammar, literature, mythology, and history. The Suda's most famous contributor, John Tzetzes, wrote about the gods of Greek mythology and provided detailed descriptions of their roles in mythological tales.

The Suda played a crucial role in preserving ancient texts and transmitting knowledge from the classical period to the Byzantine era. Its significance extends beyond its own historical context, as it has influenced later scholarly works on Byzantine culture and language.

One striking statistic about the Suda is that over 2,000 of its entries have been preserved in modern manuscripts, making it a valuable resource for historians studying Byzantine literature and linguistics.
